subject: Commercial options for Orbital Health VPC deployment
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@orbitalhealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@orbitalhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Commercial terms for VPC deployment

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency numbers and the KV caching behavior. Procurement asked me to circulate the RFP and a couple of questions to move toward term negotiation:

- Orbital prefers to defer the platform fee until month 6 of the engagement if possible (pilot months 1–5 covered by credits). Is that something Redwood will accept?
- We need a clear mapping of operator licenses vs. site/node licenses — our infra team needs to know which servers we'll be charged on for audit/compliance.
- Can you provide a redline-able SOW and the latest pricing sheet (including support tiers and on-call costs)?

I've attached the RFP for context (Orbital_RFP.pdf). Our target is to lock commercial terms by end of May.

Appreciate a quick run-down of options so we can feed to Legal.

Best,
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Cloud Ops — Orbital Health
Samantha Ortiz

Attachment: orbital_rfp.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@orbitalhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial terms for VPC deployment

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear ask and the RFP.

Short answers up front:
- Deferring the platform fee to month 6 is possible as a commercial concession, but we generally require a minimum revenue commitment or a stepped-commit schedule to protect the implementation cost.
- Operator vs. node licensing: Redwood maps operator licenses to named SRE/operators (separate seat license) or to site nodes depending on the customer preference — I'll attach a matrix showing both patterns.

I'll attach a first-pass pricing sheet and a draft SOW for your Legal to review.

Next steps I propose:
1) Kimberly and I will run two commercial options internally (standard upfront platform fee vs deferred fee + limited discount) and get back by Monday.
2) If either option is acceptable, we'll provide a DocuSign-ready SOW + pricing sheet.

I'll loop in Marissa from Sales Ops if we need sign-off on a non-standard discount.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_vpc_pricing_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), draft_sow_orbital.docx (document)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Commercial options for Orbital Health VPC deployment

Dylan — quick internal note before we send a customer-facing offer.

Context: Orbital is a strategic target (large health vertical, potential for multi-region deployment). We can be flexible on platform fee timing but need guardrails to protect Redwood:

- If we allow deferral to month 6, require: 18-month minimum term OR a 12-month commitment with a 20% operator-license floor.
- Discounting: max 12% if they accept the 18-month term and prepay months 7–12; if they want the 12-month term, cap discount at 8%. Anything beyond that needs Marissa sign-off (finance approval).
- On-call: standard SRE retainer applies; we can bake a reduced first-year on-call rate if they sign before June 15.

I've attached internal_pricing_notes.txt with the margin math and impact to NRR. If we push the deferral + >10% discount, margin drops below our threshold. Consider proposing two clean options (A/B) back to the customer so we avoid back-and-forth.

Kimberly
Head of Strategic Accounts

Attachment: internal_pricing_notes.txt (text)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@orbitalhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@orbitalhealth.com>, Orbital Health Legal <legal@orbitalhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial terms for VPC deployment — Proposal options

Samantha — thanks for waiting while we priced internally. Per our conversation, here are two tidy commercial options for Orbital to review (clean A/B to minimize legal churn):

Option A — Standard (fastest onboarding)
- Platform fee: $180k, due at kick-off (covers platform licensing & initial onboarding).
- Operator license model: Map by site nodes for your initial pilot (up to 8 nodes included); additional nodes billed monthly at $X/node.
- Support: Standard Bronze SRE retainer included for months 1–3, then standard on-call rates.
- Discount: none.
- Deliverables: DocuSign SOW (attached), pricing sheet attached.

Option B — Deferred platform fee (pilot-friendly)
- Platform fee: $180k deferred until month 6.
- Commercial guardrail: 18-month minimum term OR 12-month term + 20% operator-license floor.
- Concession: 10% discount on total platform fee if customer signs the 18-month term and prepays months 7–12; 6% discount for the 12-month + floor option.
- Operator license mapping: per-operator seat for named SREs + node-based billing for production sites beyond pilot; see attached matrix.
- Support: Reduced on-call rate for year 1 if signed by June 15.

Attachments: redwood_vpc_pricing_v1.xlsx, draft_sow_orbital.docx (DocuSign-ready after redlines).

If either looks acceptable I can convert the selected option into a DocuSign packet and route to Legal. Suggested next step: reply with preferred option (A or B) and any redline requests; if you prefer, we can schedule a 20-minute call to walk the terms.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0192
